MIZORAM PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
COMPETITIVE EXAMINATION FOR RECRUITMENT TO THE POST OF
ASSISTANT CONTROLLER OF MINES UNDER GEOLOGY & MINING,
COMMERCE & INDUSTRIES DEPARTMENT,
 GOVERNMENT OF MIZORAM.
(MARCH-2026)
GENERAL ENGLISH
Time Allowed : 3 hours
FM : 100
PART- A
(34 Marks)
This section should be answered only on the Answer Sheet provided.
Marks for each question is indicated against it. Attempt all questions.
1. Write a precis of the following passage, giving it a suitable title.
(14)
Social media has revolutionized tourism by acting as a primary source for travel inspiration,
research, and booking, with 75% of people using it to decide on destinations. Platforms like Instagram,
TikTok, and YouTube drive “Instatourism” through visual content, heavily influencing travel trends
and consumer decisions via user-generated reviews and influencer marketing.
Travelers discover new destinations, hotels, and attractions through visual storytelling,
hashtags, and geotags. Tourism businesses in their turn use these platforms for immediate interaction,
addressing queries, and improving customer service. These businesses also partner with influencers
on social media since peer reviews build trust more effectively than traditional advertising.
One effect of the boom in social media usage is the prioritization of visual aesthetics, with
millennials prioritizing a destination’s “Instagrammability”, that is, whether the planned destination is
ideal for taking photographs and videos to be uploaded on social media. While this may boost tourism
in lesser-known areas, it can lead to overtourism, environmental damage, and overcrowding when
people flock to the most trending destinations.
2. You are the Assistant Controller of Mines posted in Siaha district. Illegal mining activities have been
reported in a remote area under your jurisdiction. Preliminary verification indicates unauthorized
extraction and transportation of minerals.
Write a letter to the Director, Commerce & Industries Department, Govt. of Mizoram reporting the
situation, outlining the steps taken so far, and requesting additional manpower and technological
support to curb the illegal activity. Sign as XYZ of ABC Locality (Veng), Aizawl
(10)

3. Read the following passage, and answer the questions below:
As a kid, I spent my summers with my grandparents on their ranch in Texas… My
grandparents belonged to a Caravan Club, a group of Airstream trailer owners who travel together
around the U.S. and Canada. And every few summers, we’d join the caravan. I loved and worshipped
my grandparents and I really looked forward to these trips. On one particular trip, I was about 10
years old. I was rolling around in the big bench seat in the back of the car. My grandfather was
driving. And my grandmother had the passenger seat. She smoked throughout these trips, and I hated
the smell.
At that age, I’d take any excuse to make estimates and do minor arithmetic. I’d calculate
our gas mileage — figure out useless statistics on things like grocery spending. I’d been hearing an ad
campaign about smoking. I can’t remember the details, but basically the ad said, every puff of a
cigarette takes some number of minutes off of your life: I think it might have been two minutes per
puff. At any rate, I decided to do the math for my grandmother. I estimated the number of cigarettes
per days, estimated the number of puffs per cigarette and so on. When I was satisfied that I’d come
up with a reasonable number, I poked my head into the front of the car, tapped my grandmother on
the shoulder, and proudly proclaimed, “At two minutes per puff, you’ve taken nine years off your
life!”
I have a vivid memory of what happened, and it was not what I expected. I expected to be
applauded for my cleverness and arithmetic skills. “Jeff, you’re so smart. You had to have made
some tricky estimates, figure out the number of minutes in a year and do some division.” That’s not
what happened. Instead, my grandmother burst into tears. I sat in the backseat and did not know
what to do. While my grandmother sat crying, my grandfather, who had been driving in silence, pulled
over onto the shoulder of the highway. He got out of the car and came around and opened my door
and waited for me to follow. Was I in trouble? My grandfather was a highly intelligent, quiet man. He
had never said a harsh word to me, and maybe this was to be the first time? Or maybe he would ask
that I get back in the car and apologize to my grandmother. I had no experience in this realm with my
grandparents and no way to gauge what the consequences might be. We stopped beside the trailer.
My grandfather looked at me, and after a bit of silence, he gently and calmly said, “Jeff, one day
you’ll understand that it’s harder to be kind than clever.”
What I want to talk to you about today is the difference between gifts and choices. Cleverness
is a gift, kindness is a choice. Gifts are easy — they’re given after all. Choices can be hard. You can
seduce yourself with your gifts if you’re not careful, and if you do, it’ll probably be to the detriment of
your choices.
(Extracted from a speech given by Jeff Bezos at Princeton University, 2010)
(i) What did Bezos do that made his grandmother cry?
(2)
(ii) Why do you think Bezos’ grandfather told him that it was harder to be kind than clever?
(3)
(iii) What lesson do you think Bezos intends to impart through his story?
(3)
(iv) Find words in the passage that have the same meaning as the following:
(2)
(a) Something that happens as a result of something else
(b) A cause of harm or damage

Direction (Question Nos. 11 - 16): Complete the following statements by choosing the alternative that
best fits the context:

burden on small-scale miners.”
(a) decrease
(b) alleviate
(c) subside
(d) lessen
12. Despite the challenges, the department remained _______ in its commitment to transparency.
(a) static
(b) steadfast
(c) stationary
(d) solid

(a) momentary
(b) momentous
(c) memorable

14. The new regulation acts as a _______ for innovation, forcing companies to develop cleaner extraction
techniques to avoid heavy taxation.

(b) catalyst
(c) provocation

(b) different

(b) force
(c) mislead
(d) show

Direction (Question Nos. 27 - 36): Change the sentences by converting the underlined word as indicated:
27. The soldiers fought bravely, but they were ultimately defeated. (to noun)
(a) The soldiers fought with braveness but they were ultimately defeated.
(b) The soldiers fought with brave, but they were ultimately defeated.
(c) The soldiers fought with bravery but they were ultimately defeated.
(d) The soldiers fought bravenly but they were ultimately defeated.
28. The late arrival of the Chief Guest completely disrupted the programme. (to Verb)
(a) The late arrive of the Chief Guest completely disrupted the programme.
(b) The Chief Guest arrived late and completely disrupted the programme.
(c) The late arrived of the Chief Guest completely disrupted the programme.
(d) The Chief Guest completely disrupted the programme by his late arrivance.
29. Unluckily, we were caught in a storm. (to adjective)
(a) We were unluckily caught in a storm.
(b) It was with lack of luck that we were caught in a storm.
(c) We were unlucky to be caught in a storm.
(d) We were caught in a storm due to unlucky.

30. She handled the diplomats with great ease. (adverb)
(a) She handled the diplomats with easiness.
(b) She handled the diplomats with great easy.
(c) She handled the diplomats with easily.
(d) She handled the diplomats easily.
31. He laughed loudly, which startled the sleeping baby. (to noun)
(a) He was laughing loudly, which startled the sleeping baby.
(b) His loud laughter startled the sleeping baby
(c) His laugh was loudly, which startled the sleeping baby.
(d) He laughed in a loud manner, which startled the baby.
32. The sweetness of her voice was captivating. (to adjective)
(a) Her sweet voice was captivating
(b) Her voice captivated one sweetly
(c) She speaks sweetly and it was captivating
(d) Her voice is sweet and is captivating.
33. I want you to be firm in holding on to your beliefs. (adverb)
(a) I want you to hold on to your beliefs firmly
(b) I want you to have firmness in holding on to your beliefs
(c) I want you to have a firm manner in holding on to your beliefs
(d) I want you to be firmly in holding on to your beliefs,
34. Even among a crowd, she felt lonely. (to noun)
(a) Even among a crowd, she felt alone.
(b) Even among a crowd, she felt aloneness.
(c) Even among a crowd, she felt lonesome
(d) Even among a crowd, she felt a sense of loneliness.
35. He was wrongly accused of theft. (adjective)
(a) He faced a wrong accusation of theft
(b) He was accused of theft in a wrong manner.
(c) He was wronged by the accusation of theft.
(d) It was a wrong accusation of theft.
36. I take great pride in your achievements. (to adjective)
(a) I feel prideness in your achievements
(b) I am proud in your achievements
(c) I feel proudly about your achievements
(d) I am very proud of your achievements

Direction (Question Nos. 47 - 51): Choose the correct answer from the given alternatives:
47. The officer said to the worker, “Show me your permit.”
(a) The officer ordered the worker to show him his permit.
(b) The officer said to the worker to show him his permit.
(c) The officer ordered the worker that he show him his permit.
(d) The officer told the worker show me your permit.
48. He said to me, “Don’t enter the restricted area.”
(a) He said to me not to enter the restricted area.
(b) He told me that I don’t enter the restricted area.
(c) He warned me not to enter the restricted area.
(d) He suggested me to not enter the restricted area.
49. The supervisor ordered the workers to wear their safety helmets.
(a) The supervisor said, “Workers, you must wear safety helmets.”
(b) The supervisor said to the workers, “Wear your safety helmets.”
(c) The supervisor said, “Workers wore their safety helmets.”
(d) The supervisor told, “Please wear your safety helmets.”
50. The father warned his son not to waste his time.
(a) The father said to his son, “You should not waste your time.”
(b) The father said to his son, “Don’t waste your time.”
(c) The father said, “Not to waste your time.”
(d) The father told his son, “Don’t waste my time.”
51. “I have submitted the report,” said the clerk.
(a) The clerk said that he had submitted the report.
(b) The clerk said that he has submitted the report.
(c) The clerk said that he submitted the report.
(d) The clerk told he had submitted the report.
